findings.title: Temporary for an array `==` operand is hoisted out of a `while` condition: the condition's side effect runs once, giving an infinite loop / wrong round count
findings.why: `pfLine` writes into the statement prefix, and `genStmtInner`'s ST_WHILE case (codegen.c:4053-4056) calls `flushPrefix(g)` *before* emitting `while (...)`, so the temporary is evaluated exactly once, outside the loop, while the loop condition keeps reading it. The invariant that a prefix may be hoisted is only enforced for `??`: `check_stmt.c:894` raises `c->noHoist` for a `while` condition and `check_expr.c:2624` rejects `??` there with "the temporary would run once instead of every round". `eqOperand` (reached from genBin's array-equality branch at line 1295 -> genEqCall) has no such guard, so a condition whose operand is a call keeps comparing against the first result forever. The comment at 1208-1209 ("Both sides are evaluated exactly once and in source order") is violated: the call may run zero more times.
findings.trigger: A `while` condition containing `==`/`!=` on an array (the only type genEqCall is used for) where at least one operand is not a place: a function call, an array/struct literal, a `dyn` value, etc. Equivalent hoisting applies to the other prefix producers (genMethodCall's dyn slot/payload temporaries, genPrint, EX_NEW, parallel::run), which have the same missing guard.

findings.title: genViewCopier (`copyInto`'s primitive) dereferences a NULL storage pointer: it lacks the `!v.data` guard that the index primitive has
findings.why: The sibling primitive genViewIndexer (codegen.c:742) emits `if (!v.data) extc_trapMsg(file, line, "the view has no storage");` because the state `len > 0 && data == NULL` is reachable and was found by the project's own fuzzer (tests/traps/view_no_storage.extc, whose comment records `extc_pool_take` returning nothing while the slice still claimed length 4). `_copy` performs the same element access but validates only the counts, so `memmove(d.data, s.data, n*sizeof(T))` reads/writes through NULL. The `_index`/`_copy` pair is generated by the same request mechanism (viewIndexer/viewCopier, lines 796-811) and is used for the same slices, so the asymmetry is not an invariant established elsewhere.
findings.trigger: `copyInto<T>(dstView, srcView, n)` with n>0 where either view has NULL data and a length >= n - i.e. exactly the shape of tests/traps/view_no_storage.extc, which uses an index instead of a copy.

findings.title: genBin wraps a `ref` right operand in `&(...)` without checking whether the operand is already a reference: `a == ref b` emits `&(&(b))`
findings.why: The left operand is converted by selfOperandAsParam, which distinguishes all four combinations of (parameter is `ref`) x (operand already is a reference) and only takes an address when the generated C is not already a pointer. The right operand is only inspected through the *parameter* type, so when the source operand is itself a reference expression (`ref b`, whose genExpr is `&(b)`) the emitted C is `&(&(b))` - not valid C. The checker accepts and in fact recommends that spelling for a reference parameter ("argument expects `ref ...`; write `ref ...` here to pass a reference").
findings.trigger: Any overloaded comparison operator (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) whose second parameter is declared `ref T`, called with an explicit reference argument: `if a == ref b { }`.

findings.title: opOverloadSuffix derives the overload suffix from the *caller's* substitution context, so a generic method's definition and its call site get different C names
findings.why: `subst(g, p1->type)` uses whatever monomorphization context is current. When the method is emitted as part of the instance `w<i32>`, substEnter has set T->i32, so cFuncName produces `w_i32_eq_i32`. A call site in a non-generic function has no context, so the same FuncDef yields `ttMangle(T)` = "T" and cMethodName produces `w_i32_eq_T`. The definition is then unreferenced (and dropped by dropUnreferenced), and the emitted C calls a function that does not exist. Definition and call site must agree on the name; the invariant is established nowhere else, and in fact cMethodName's own comment warns that the callee may belong to a different instantiation than the one being generated.
findings.trigger: A generic owner with two methods of the same operator name (allowed once per right-operand type, check_top.c:157) where at least one of them takes a type parameter in the second-parameter position, and a call site outside any generic instance context (e.g. plain `main`).

findings.title: genGlobalInit makes only the outermost struct literal a brace initializer: a nested literal stays a compound literal, which is not a valid static initializer
findings.why: `staticInit` is not propagated: a field whose value is another struct literal is generated with `genExpr`, i.e. genStructLit -> genStructLitAs(..., false), which spells `(T){...}`. In a file-scope object's initializer C11 6.7.9p4 requires constant expressions, and a compound literal is not one, so the documented intent of genStructLitAs ("The brace form is the same list, so the spelling differs by exactly that prefix") holds only one level deep. gcc accepts the file-scope compound literal as an extension, so --check-c stays green; a pedantic build does not.
findings.trigger: A global (file-scope `var`/`let`) initialized with a struct literal that contains another struct literal as a field value.

findings.title: C keywords are renamed only for functions/methods: a struct/enum type name or a global variable named after a keyword is emitted verbatim and the generated C does not compile
findings.why: cSymName (574-588) exists precisely to keep a user name that collides with a C keyword out of the generated C (`fn double(...)` becomes `double__c`, and the checker renames locals/parameters), but it is only consulted from cFuncName/cMethodName. Nominal type names (`t->name` here, and the typedef/enum definitions emitted later) and global variable names bypass it, so a legal extC identifier that is a C keyword produces a declaration the C compiler cannot parse while extc exits 0. Only --check-c notices.
findings.trigger: Any nominal type or global whose name is a C keyword: `struct double {...}`, `type int = | a | b`, `var int: i32 = 3` (locals and parameters are already renamed and work).
findings.repro:
files /tmp/rev/work/m_kw1.extc (`struct double { x: i32 }` + `var d: double = { x: 1 }`), m_kw3.extc (`var int: i32 = 3`), m_kw4.extc (`type int = | a | b`); each compiles with exit 0 and then:
  gcc -fsyntax-only m_kw1.c -> "typedef struct double double;" error: expected '{' before 'double'
  gcc -fsyntax-only m_kw3.c -> "static int32_t int = 3;" error: two or more data types in declaration specifiers
  gcc -fsyntax-only m_kw4.c -> "typedef enum { int_a = 0, int_b = 1 } int;" error: expected ';', identifier or '(' before 'int'
For contrast m_kw2.extc (a parameter and a local both named after keywords) produces C that gcc accepts.

findings.title: The operator-as-method-call path never passes `@overwrite` cells, unlike the three other call emitters (currently latent: owLocal is always true today)
findings.why: A call to a function with `owSites > 0 && !owLocal` must pass one `extc_owcell *` per site; the signature emitter makes those parameters mandatory (codegen.c:4298-4303: `extc_owcell *__extc_owarg%d`) and the other three emitters do pass them - EX_METHOD at line 1999, EX_CALL at line 2471, EX_ASSOC at line 2569, all through owPassCells (3607-3613). genBin calls only cgImplicitArgs, so an operator method in that state is called with too few arguments (invalid C behind exit 0). The comment right above claims the opposite invariant ("an operator **is** a method call, so it asks the same single owner everything else asks"), which is what makes this a divergence rather than a decision. I could not construct a trigger: check_top.c:6243 sets `owLocal = true` for every function the checker enumerates and instances copy the template's value, so EXTC_DUMP_OW=1 reports `local=1` everywhere (checked on generic methods and free functions), no corpus file mentions `__extc_owarg`, and a generic method with an `@overwrite` site was emitted without the hidden parameter. So the missing call is dead today; it is reported because the branch is documented as live for codegen-created instances and the divergence is one line of duplicated convention.
findings.trigger: Would need a FuncDef with owSites > 0 and owLocal == false reached through an overloaded operator; not reachable with the current checker (verified as described).
findings.repro: Not reproducible. Tried: (a) `fn +(self: ref box, v: i64) -> box` with `@overwrite var x = new node` called as `b + i64(5)` (/tmp/rev/work/c_owop.extc) - the generated signature was `static box box_add(box * self, int64_t v)`, i.e. owLocal was already true; (b) the same on a generic struct instance (c_owgen2.extc) - `EXTC_DUMP_OW=1` prints `[ow] == sites=1 local=1`; (c) grep of tests/examples for `owarg` - no hits.

coverage_notes: Read all of src/codegen.c lines 1-2150 (plus surrounding call sites elsewhere in the file and in check_expr.c/check_stmt.c/check_top.c/types.c where an invariant had to be verified). Functions read line by line: cgFormat/cgLine/pfLine/flushPrefix, subst/substEnter/substLeave, cType/fnParamList, cSymName/exportName/opOverloadSuffix/cFuncName/cMethodName, isView/isByteView, genViewIndexer/genViewCopier and viewIndexer/viewCopier, needDesc/needEq/descRef/deadDefAdd, genStructDesc/genArrayDesc/genViewDesc/genEnumDesc, emitDescDefs/eqNeeded/closeEqNeeds/emitDescRegion, findOpMethod/eqOperand/genEqCall/genEqAdapter, genBin, zeroValue/zeroInit/needsExplicitZero/nullValue/elemBraces/substEnterInst, printArgIsPlace/genPrint, cgHasImplicitArgs/cgImplicitArgs, selfOperandAsParam/genDynValue/genMethodCall, litValueFor/genStructLitAs/genStructLit/genGlobalInit, and the head of genExprInner (EX_EXT/EX_LAMBDA/EX_INT/EX_FLOAT/EX_STR/EX_IDENT/EX_FIELD/EX_CALL dispatching). Checked as correct (or verified sound by testing): eqOperand's temp/place split for non-loop positions (if/assign/return), the descriptor demand closure incl. cycles and the byte-view/slice_u8 special case, genEqAdapter's ref/value parameter handling, genStructDesc's offsetof use (C members live in their own namespace, keyword-looking field names are fine - verified with `struct s { double: i32  int: i32 }`), genArrayDesc's element stride for nested arrays, zeroValue's brace counts for arrays/structs/generic instances (compared against gcc -Wmissing-braces for [N]i32, [N][M]i32, arrays of structs and of payload enums), selfOperandAsParam's four ref/value combinations and its one-element-array trick, genMethodCall's coroutine-handle and dyn protocols (the vtable/payload names agree between emitter and call site, verified with a generic dyn payload), the `?`/EX_EXT prefix flushes, and the arena/zone arguments of the operator path (setOpCallArgs does set zoneLevel/arenaArg on the bin node; an operator method that allocates gets the same `__extc_home` the definition declares). Also confirmed non-issues: `@export` on a generic function is rejected by the checker; printing a `fn` value is rejected; a `ref`-typed operand is rejected; `??` inside a while condition is rejected. Not covered here (outside lines 1-2150): statements/loops emission, function prologues/epilogues, the runtime blocks, dyn table emission and dropUnreferenced (read only to check the invariant my findings depend on).
